feedback:
Written before this candidate races, so no outcome is stated for it. The candidate is valid: five 8 mm sensors at x = -0.02, -0.01, 0, 0.01, 0.02 and y = 0.03 are inside the allowed ranges, the weights are antisymmetric in [-2, 2], and kp, ki, kd, base_speed and line_loss are in range. Nothing is obviously broken.

The change is relative to iteration 4 (best raced, 91.4). Iteration 5 (seven sensors to ±0.024, same kp, ki and kd as iteration 4) scored 89.5. Iterations 0 to 5 all ended off_track on every trial, with max_error at 0.061 to 0.064 and 1 to 2 line-loss events per run. Span has been tested at ±0.016 and ±0.024, but not at ±0.02, so this is a fair intermediate step.

Three changes are confounded in one race. (1) The span widens to ±0.02. (2) The weights ±2 over ±0.02 give about 100 per metre, against about 125 per metre in iteration 4, so the effective steering gain is about 20 percent lower, as it was in iteration 5. (3) kd rises from 0.3 to 0.45 at kp 3.0. The rationale does not mention the lower gain. Iteration 1 showed kd 0.2 at kp 2.0 raising steering_oscillation (0.10 to 0.20), so the kd rise needs watching. Base_speed 1.2 also works against progress: iteration 4 at 1.3 reached 0.44 on oval, and the course needs about 1.5 m/s to finish.

I am approving rather than revising. The design is valid and close to the best raced design, all candidates so far have failed in the same way, and telemetry from this race will separate the span effect from the kd effect better than another review on numbers alone. Next step depends on the race. If line_loss_events fall but max_error stays at or above 0.06, raise kp before adding kd, as iteration 4 suggested. If steering_oscillation rises well above 0.25 with kd 0.45, bring kd back to 0.3. If progress on oval falls below iteration 4's 0.44 while the line is held, restore base_speed to 1.3 or 1.5.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events are 1 or fewer but max_error stays at or above 0.06, raise kp from 3.0 toward 3.5 with the sensors and kd held, because iterations 0 to 5 show line loss at bends rather than oscillation (steering_oscillation about 0.1 to 0.2).
If steering_oscillation rises clearly above about 0.25 with kd 0.45, lower kd to 0.3, since iteration 1 showed kd 0.2 raising jitter and the wider signal may amplify it.
If the robot holds the line but oval progress stays below iteration 4's 0.44, restore base_speed to 1.3 or 1.5, because the lower speed of 1.2 costs progress and the course needs about 1.5 m/s.
